title: Two caption lines join into one, and a word moves back to the line before
goal: Automatic captions sometimes break a sentence in the wrong place. Today a word can be pushed to the next line but never pulled back, and two short lines cannot be joined. Let a person join a caption line with the next one, and move a word back to the line before, from the word's right-click menu.
notes: Word menu: Sources/Photonz/EditorState+CaptionWords.swift:182-197 (Edit Word, Split Here, Merge with Next which merges WORDS inside one line, Delete Word, Move to Next Line -> document.moveCaptionWordsToNextCue). Menu bar rows: EditorCommands.swift:1388-1390. No cue-level join exists (grep join/merge cue finds nothing). Mock: docs/design/mocks/pages/video-captions.html (editing in place). Premiere: Merge Captions. Success item for video-audio: captions 'can be edited in place'. Found by the 2026-10-05 evening manager pass's captions comparison.
acceptance: Right-click on a caption word offers Move to Previous Line (on any word, taking it and every word before it on that line), beside the existing Move to Next Line
Right-click on a caption line on the captions track offers Join with Next Line, which makes one line from the two with every word's timing kept, in one undo step
Both rows are in the menu bar where the existing caption word rows are, and are dimmed where they cannot act (the first line has no previous one, the last no next)

A walk at Next defaults lets captions write themselves on the sample talk, joins two lines and moves a word back, and reads the line count and words after each; it runs green, and SRT export shows the joined line
Try it: open a talking recording, let the captions write, right-click the first word of the second line, Move to Previous Line. Audit written under queue/audits/
anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar, and written into this task's log if it does not
